questions.question: Lord Kapila compares a person engaged in material consciousness, who does not know the strength of the time factor carrying him, to what?

options.text: A mass of clouds that does not know the influence of the wind
A blind man in a well

questions.explanation: "As a mass of clouds does not know the powerful influence of the wind, a person engaged in material consciousness does not know the powerful strength of the time factor, by which he is being carried." (SB 3.30.1)

questions.question: Whatever is produced by the materialist with great pain for so-called happiness is destroyed by the Supreme Personality as the time factor, and for this reason the conditioned soul does what?
questions.explanation: "Whatever is produced by the materialist with great pain and labor for so-called happiness, the Supreme Personality, as the time factor, destroys, and for this reason the conditioned soul laments." (SB 3.30.2)

questions.question: What does the misguided materialist fail to understand about his body, home, land and wealth?

options.text: That they are gifts of the Lord
That they are impermanent and temporary
That they are sources of merit
That they belong to the demigods

questions.explanation: "The misguided materialist does not know that his very body is impermanent and that the attractions of home, land and wealth, which are in relationship to that body, are also temporary." (SB 3.30.3)

questions.question: According to Lord Kapila, why is the conditioned living entity satisfied with his own particular species of life, even when in hell?

options.text: Because of the mode of goodness
Because he is deluded by the covering influence of the illusory energy

questions.explanation: "The conditioned living entity is satisfied in his own particular species of life; while deluded by the covering influence of the illusory energy, he feels little inclined to cast off his body, even when in hell, for he takes delight in hellish enjoyment." (SB 3.30.5)

questions.question: Satisfaction with one's standard of living is due to deep-rooted attraction for body, wife, home, children, animals, wealth and what?
questions.explanation: "Such satisfaction with one's standard of living is due to deep-rooted attraction for body, wife, home, children, animals, wealth and friends." (SB 3.30.6)

questions.question: To whom does the attached householder give his heart and senses, becoming falsely charmed?

options.text: A woman who charms him with maya

questions.explanation: "He gives heart and senses to a woman, who falsely charms him with maya." (SB 3.30.8)

questions.question: How does the attached householder use the money he secures by committing violence here and there?

options.text: He gives it all in charity
He himself eats only a little portion and goes to hell for those for whom he earned it
He offers it to the demigods

questions.explanation: "He secures money by committing violence here and there, and although he employs it in the service of his family, he himself eats only a little portion of the food thus purchased, and he goes to hell for those for whom he earned the money in such an irregular way." (SB 3.30.10)

questions.question: When the unsuccessful family man is unable to support them, how do his wife and others treat him?

options.text: They do not treat him with the same respect as before

questions.explanation: "Seeing him unable to support them, his wife and others do not treat him with the same respect as before, even as miserly farmers do not accord the same treatment to their old and worn-out oxen." (SB 3.30.13)

questions.question: How does the foolish family man, maintained by those whom he once maintained, remain at home in old age?

options.text: Like a pet dog, eating whatever is negligently given to him

questions.explanation: "Thus he remains at home just like a pet dog and eats whatever is so negligently given to him." (SB 3.30.15)

questions.question: In the diseased condition described by Kapila, what sound does the dying man produce within his throat upon breathing?
questions.explanation: "He has difficulty breathing, and upon exhaling and inhaling he produces a sound like ghura-ghura, a rattling within the throat." (SB 3.30.16)

questions.question: At the time of death, when he sees the messengers of the lord of death with eyes full of wrath, what does the sinful man do in great fear?
questions.explanation: "At death, he sees the messengers of the lord of death come before him, their eyes full of wrath, and in great fear he passes stool and urine." (SB 3.30.19)

questions.question: What are the messengers who arrest a person engaged in criminal sense gratification called?
questions.explanation: "A person engaged in criminal sense gratification is similarly arrested by the Yamadutas, who bind him by the neck with strong rope and cover his subtle body so that he may undergo severe punishment." (SB 3.30.20)

questions.question: How great a distance does the punished soul have to pass within two or three moments on the way to Yamaraja?
questions.explanation: "Thus he has to pass ninety-nine thousand yojanas within two or three moments, and then he is at once engaged in the torturous punishment which he is destined to suffer." (SB 3.30.24)

questions.question: Into which hells are men and women whose lives were built upon indulgence in illicit sex life put?
questions.explanation: "Men and women whose lives were built upon indulgence in illicit sex life are put into many kinds of miserable conditions in the hells known as Tamisra, Andha-tamisra and Raurava." (SB 3.30.28)

questions.question: What does the man who maintained himself and his family by sinful activities carry with him as passage money when he leaves this world?

options.text: The money he acquired by envying other living entities

questions.explanation: "He goes alone to the darkest regions of hell after quitting the present body, and the money he acquired by envying other living entities is the passage money with which he leaves this world." (SB 3.30.31)

questions.question: A person eager to maintain his family and kinsmen by black methods certainly goes to which darkest region of hell?
questions.explanation: "Therefore a person who is very eager to maintain his family and kinsmen simply by black methods certainly goes to the darkest region of hell, which is known as Andha-tamisra." (SB 3.30.33)

questions.question: After being purged of his sins through hellish conditions and lower animal life, where is one reborn?

options.text: As a human being on this earth

questions.explanation: "Having thus been purged of his sins, one is reborn again as a human being on this earth." (SB 3.30.34)
